content:
We got search results: two templates. Need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction. Likely use carbonyl-ene reaction (retro direction: break C-O and C-C to form C=O and C=C). So we need a template that does forward carbonyl-ene (i.e., product is our target). The retro step would be applying that template to target to get precursors: a ketone and an alkene (maybe a cyclopentanol?). The search gave template 1229769 which seems to involve a silyl group? Not ideal. Template 1209837 is simpler: retro_smarts: '[C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]'. This looks like forward: carbonyl-ene? Actually forward: product (right side) is C-C(=C)-C(=O)-O... hmm. The retro direction (apply to product) would give a carbonyl-ene precursor: an alkene and a carbonyl? The product side includes a hydroxyl attached to carbon 1? Let's interpret: The template maps a substrate with OH (alcohol) to a product with C=C and C=O. So applying retro (i.e., using template to go from product to precursors) would break C-O and C-C to form C=O and C=C. That's what we need.

Thus we can use template_id 1209837. Need to apply to our target molecule. Use apply_template to get precursors.
